samples.summary: The frontend YorkieDocStore read boundary — the live collaborative path this change exists for — gets no test for any of the new bands
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` gains its own copies of the guards (`normalizeFontSize` at the inline parse, `isPaintableImageSize`, `normalizeCellPadding` in `parseCellStyle`, `normalizeRowHeight` on the `rowHeights` attribute, `normalizeListLevel` on `listLevel`). This is a *duplicate* parser from `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts`, and only the docs-package copy is covered (`packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts` and `row-height.test.ts`/`list-level.test.ts` all call `treeNodeToBlock` from `../../src/model/crdt-tree.js`). Grepping `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` for `listLevel|rowHeights|fontSize|padding|image.width|normalize` finds only happy-path values (fontSize 14/18/20, listLevel 0/1) — no `Infinity`, `NaN`, `1e9` or negative case anywhere in `packages/frontend/tests` for these attributes. So if a band is wired to the wrong field, dropped, or inverted in the frontend copy, nothing fails: frontend also has no `tsc` lane, and the two parsers can silently drift. The frontend copy is the one that actually reads a hostile peer's attributes in production.

samples.summary: New public `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` has no direct test, and the header/footer-table-cell case that motivates it is uncovered
samples.evidence: `siblingBlocksOf` (and the new `walkCellsForSiblings`) are new public model API; `grep siblingBlocksOf packages/docs/test` returns nothing, so there is no unit test in `test/model/document.test.ts`. The editor tests in `test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts` cover a *body* table cell, a stale/deleted parent-map entry, and a *top-level* header list — but never a caret inside a header or footer **table cell**, which is precisely the case the code comments in `editor.ts:1624` and `text-editor.ts:2909` cite as the reason for switching from `layout.blockParentMap` to `doc.siblingBlocksOf` (a header-cell caret resolving to `undefined` in the body layout map would make the whole indent gesture a silent no-op). The footer branches of `siblingBlocksOf` are likewise unexercised.

samples.summary: The new non-termination guard for a degenerate `pageSetup` (`if (!(fragHeight > 0)) fragHeight = remaining`) is never exercised
samples.evidence: The guard's stated purpose is `contentHeight <= 0` from a degenerate page setup, where the preceding line would produce a negative fragment and walk `consumed` backwards forever. Every pagination test added by this diff uses `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` (`test/model/row-height.test.ts`, `test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts` both do `const setup = DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`), so `contentHeight` is always ~864 px and this branch is dead in the suite; `test/view/pagination.test.ts` also only uses `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` (line 441). A regression here is a hung tab, and nothing would catch it. Also unexercised: `paginatableRowHeight`'s `if (!(contentHeight > 0)) return raw;` early return.
searchedFor: Read new pagination tests in row-height.test.ts and numeric-attrs.test.ts

samples.summary: The PDF painter's two new `normalizeListLevel` call sites are untested
samples.evidence: `pdf-painter.ts` now normalizes `block.listLevel` for both the body marker x (line ~367) and the table-cell list-counter key (line ~593), justified by 'a poisoned one … would put NaN coordinates into pdf-lib'. `grep listLevel|rowHeights|fontSize packages/docs/test/export/pdf-painter.test.ts` finds no matches, and no test in `packages/docs/test/export/` feeds a NaN/Infinity/out-of-band `listLevel` through an export. The layout-side equivalents are covered (list-level.test.ts asserts finite geometry via `computeTableLayout`), but the export path has no analogous assertion, so a raw read reintroduced there ships silently.

samples.summary: The paint-side list-level normalizations (doc-canvas, paint-layout, table-renderer, peer-cursor) have no poisoned-level coverage
samples.evidence: Four render/caret sites now call `normalizeListLevel` with comments about 'a NaN x is a caret that never paints' and 'a `Map` key … would never match itself'. `grep -l 'NaN|Infinity|1e9' packages/docs/test/view` returns only `text-box-editor.test.ts`, `editor-page-setup.test.ts`, `decoration-index.test.ts` — none of the marker/caret suites (`render-list-marker.test.ts`, `paint-layout.test.ts`, `table-renderer`-related, `peer-cursor.test.ts`) pass an out-of-band `listLevel`. The correctness claim (paint agrees with the clamped layout indent) is therefore asserted only in prose.

samples.summary: The text-box editor's new `doc.batch()` wrapping (one undo unit) and its non-list marginLeft branch are not asserted
samples.evidence: `text-box-editor.ts` `indent()`/`outdent()` now wrap `applyListLevelChanges` in `doc.batch()` with the comment 'Batched so it stays one undo unit'. The only new text-box test (`test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts`, the `indent / outdent carry a list item's nested children` case) asserts only the final committed `listLevel` array — it never undoes, and never checks batching or that a plain paragraph in the same selection still gets `marginLeft`. The docs editor equivalent is properly covered by `TracingStore` (`writeDepths`, `canUndo()` false after one undo) in `editor-tab-bullet.test.ts`; the text-box path has no equivalent, so an unbatched regression there (half-moved subtree on one Cmd+Z) would pass.
searchedFor: Grep TracingStore/canUndo usage (present only in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts)

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (the array form) is exported but has no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `grep -rn normalizeRowHeights` matches only its own definition at `packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts:42`. It is not re-exported from `index.ts`/`node.ts` in this diff and `test/model/row-height.test.ts` only imports `normalizeRowHeight` and `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT`, so the helper is entirely uncovered dead code.
